statements.markdown: For the converse, take the verifier and bounds $p,\alpha,\beta$ of Theorem 1.1, guess the first $p(n)$ proof bits and simulate the verifier, in polynomial time, on each of the at most $2^\beta(2(n+2))^\alpha$ random strings. Perfect completeness gives a prefix accepted on every run. If such a prefix existed for a no-instance, its zero extension would have acceptance probability one, contradicting soundness. The resulting witness relation is decidable in polynomial time, so the language lies in NP.
